test: Compute per year: timecard hours (regular+overtime) and labour-entry hours for hourly employees, unclocked share = (paid - clocked)/paid. Break down by role and by employee (employee-year clocked/paid ratio), check whether growth is in a subset of employees/roles or spread evenly; check composition shift (role mix, new hires vs tenured, employees with no labour entries at all); check against job load (orders/jobs/estimated hours per year) and the 2025 overtime stop; check annual aggregation to remove week-alignment artefacts.
support: Unclocked share rises within a few roles or a minority of employees (their clocked/paid ratio falls over time) while others stay flat, and the rise isn't explained by job volume falling or by headcount mix.
weaken: Share rises similarly across roles and employees (a general shift, e.g. falling job load / idle capacity or a recording change), or the rise is explained by composition (more indirect-role or new-hire hours), or it disappears when computed annually.
expect: Moderate confidence the rise is real at annual grain (so not a week-alignment artefact). I expect it to be largely spread across direct roles and to track job load (clocked hours fall while paid hours stay flat), i.e. idle capacity rather than concentrated in a few people; maybe 35% chance it concentrates in particular roles/employees.
